newsitem.title: USA: New York phone users set for $15 rebate.
newsitem.headline: New York phone users set for $15 rebate.

text.p: The New York Public Service Commission Wednesday ordered Nynex Corp. to return a total $109.6 million to customers in the state, which would work out to a $15 rebate on every bill.

Nynex said it and the Commission reached a comprehensive settlement of several long-standing issues rather than drag them out any longer where they might interfere with the company's merger with Bell Atlantic Corp.
The commission said $87 million is for improper dealings with affiliates between 1984 and 1991, and $22.6 million was for quality of service rebates.
However, the commission said that Nynex improved its performance on all 16 quality measures in the last quarter of 1996 compared with the year-earlier period.
"The commission's focus on service quality and the company's willingness to devote the necessary resources have produced significant results," commission Chairman John O'Mara said.
"This is a day that Nynex saw final closure of a number of long standing issues," Nynex spokesman Bob Varettoni said.
"While we did pay a high price to clear the decks, we are now moving forward to the exciting opportunities that await us," Varettoni said.
New York Telephone, which is Nynex's operating company in the state, had about $8 billion in revenues in 1996.

The affiliates case began in 1990 when the commission said New York Telephone had been overcharged by another Nynex unit, Nynex Material Enterprises Co., for removing telephone switches and related equipment.
This and another case, over rates charged by Nynex Information Resources to New York Telephone, went to court but by November 1996 had not been resolved.
Instead Nynex and the commission have made an agreement that includes clauses to stop these types of affiliate transactions from occurring, the commission said.

Nynex will refund $53 million plus interest for the Nynex Material Enterprises case, and $30 million plus interest for the Nynex Information Resources case. This totals $87 million, is to be credited on consumer bills within 90 days.
The quality of service rebates concern a regulatory plan which began in 1995 to replace rate of return regulation with a system of price controls and quality hurdles.

Nynex said that the commission had not yet decided how the rebates will be distributed, but if it is distributed equally among customers it could average $14.70 for the 7.5 million customers the company has in New York.
Nynex, which expects to finalise its merger with Bell Atlantic at the end of the quarter, said it had established reserves to cover all the rebates, and there would be no effect on earnings.
